title: Onset of a quantum Fisher-Selke sequence in the transverse-field ANNNI model and its bilayer
authors: Tuan-Vu Truong, Vu-Quoc-Minh Nguyen, Hoang-Long Nguyen, Thanh-Tien Nguyen
abstract: We study the transverse-field axial next-nearest-neighbor Ising (ANNNI) model on the square lattice and on a bilayer. At the classical multiphase point $κ=J_2/J_0=1/2$, every configuration of straight domain walls that separates domains of at least two sites is a ground state. The walls are rigid, so perturbation theory in the transverse field $g=Γ/J_0$ can be carried out for each configuration separately, and we take it to order $g^8$. Quantum fluctuations select $\langle 3\rangle$ ($\uparrow\uparrow\uparrow\downarrow\downarrow\downarrow$) at order $g^2$, because spins next to a wall gain the most energy from virtual flips. The structures $\langle 23\rangle$, $\langle 223\rangle$ and $\langle 2223\rangle$ then open between $\langle 3\rangle$ and the antiphase $\langle 2\rangle$ at orders $g^4$, $g^6$ and $g^8$, in the order of the Fisher-Selke sequence of the classical three-dimensional model. A second layer suppresses each successive phase more strongly, beyond the stiffening of the local fields. We test the two widest phases with stochastic series expansion quantum Monte Carlo, comparing the free energies of the competing ordered states by thermodynamic integration, since annealing freezes in the modulation that forms at the ordering transition. The simulations reproduce the $\langle 3\rangle$ wedge to about 1%, and in a pre-registered test $\langle 23\rangle$ is stable at six of seven points, with the seventh resolved by post-hoc runs.
summary: This work analyzes the phase diagram of the transverse-field ANNNI model, demonstrating how quantum fluctuations drive the system through a sequence of ordered magnetic phases analogous to the Fisher-Selke sequence. By combining high-order perturbation theory with advanced quantum Monte Carlo simulations, the authors confirm the stability and relative ordering of these phases, particularly noting the unique suppression effect observed in the bilayer extension.
main_problem: The study investigates the onset and stability of various ordered magnetic structures within the transverse-field Axial Next-Nearest-Neighbor Ising (ANNNI) model, both on a single layer and in a bilayer.
main_result: Quantum fluctuations select a sequence of ordered phases ($\langle 3 angle$, $\langle 23 angle$, etc.) whose emergence follows the pattern of the classical Fisher-Selke sequence, with the bilayer structure suppressing these successive phases.
method: The research combines high-order perturbation theory in the transverse field ($g$) with Stochastic Series Expansion (SSE) quantum Monte Carlo simulations to calculate free energies and compare competing ordered states.
model_or_system: The system is the transverse-field ANNNI model defined on a square lattice, extended to a bilayer. The Hamiltonian includes nearest-neighbor and next-nearest-neighbor Ising interactions, along with a transverse field term ($\Gamma \sum \sigma^x$).
key_observables: Energy per spin ($e$), transverse magnetization ($m_x$), and the free energies of competing ordered states ($\langle 3 angle$, $\langle 2 angle$, $\langle 23 angle$).
important_parameters: The critical parameters include the ratio of next-nearest-neighbor to nearest-neighbor coupling ($\kappa = J_2/J_0$) and the transverse field strength ($g = \Gamma/J_0$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on perturbation theory up to $g^8$ and rigorous comparison of simulation results across multiple lattice sizes and simulation protocols to establish phase stability.
figures_summary: The notes refer to figures illustrating the low-field phase diagram near the multiphase point, showing crossings and the stability windows for different ordered phases.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the classical ground state degeneracy at $\kappa=1/2$. It then uses perturbation theory to determine the leading quantum corrections, identifying the sequence of phases ($\langle 3 angle 	o \langle 23 angle 	o \dots$). Finally, it uses quantum Monte Carlo simulations to confirm these theoretical predictions, especially in the bilayer geometry.
why_interesting: The connection between quantum fluctuations and the emergence of sequences mirroring classical critical phenomena (Fisher-Selke sequence) in an extended magnetic model is highly relevant for understanding quantum phase transitions in lattice systems.
